data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes its subject when the guard's predicate is written against the subject's declared interface rather than its executable behavior, so any mutation that adds behavior without altering declared data passes through untested and the test's coverage claim becomes a tautology over the declaration.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3-of-26 survivors can be distinguished by their declared-data signatures from the killed mutations, then the guard is not merely checking declarations.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If at least one surviving mutation changes executable behavior but is killed in an isolated run where the declaration space is reset between mutations, the tautology claim is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 compile.py survivor alters the compile output byte-for-byte, then its survival is not explained by declared-data blindness.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4-to-6/7 module variation disappears when declaration and behavior are checked by separate guards, the mechanism is refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The three survivors are one bug in two costumes: guards check declared data (registry entries, type metadata, rule records) but do not execute the mutated behavior. When installation is shown-to-fail-first, the first failure saturates the shared declaration space, so later mutations inherit a registry state that either rejects them outright or makes their declared-data signature indistinguishable from the already-failed baseline. The test then constrains the subject by fixing the declaration space in advance; it does not describe the subject because the executable difference of each mutation is never exercised.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
